page.title: Evidence
page.purpose: Prove or disprove each claim with its capture: the screenshot and accessibility-tree evidence behind every verdict, per state.

priorities.statement: The pairing of verdict and evidence is unmistakable — a verdict is never separated from what produced it.
The capture (screenshot) and the accessibility tree are jointly inspectable.
A failing claim leads to a next action, not a dead end.

states.description: Captures exist; verdicts render beside their evidence.
No captures yet for this page (BAS never ran or was unavailable); explains how to produce them and that skips are not failures.
Evidence predates the current spec revision; verdicts shown but visibly outdated.

elements.name: Page capture
elements.description: The BAS screenshot for the selected page/state.

elements.name: Accessibility tree
elements.description: The captured a11y tree, focusable per node.

elements.name: Claim verdicts
elements.description: Per-claim verdict with tier and timestamp.
Per-verdict control that focuses the tree node / capture region that produced it.

claims.statement: The page capture is present with a meaningful accessible name identifying page and state.
Claim verdicts are exposed as a list with tier and timestamp per entry.
No verdict is shown without a working link to the capture region or tree node that produced it — the house principle.
claims.rationale: Attested per release until the evidence linkage is mechanically traversable; then promoted to machine.

claims.statement: Every evidence link is keyboard reachable from its verdict.
claims.rationale: BAS v1 AX joins do not reliably expose this repeated per-verdict focus control as default-state evidence; keep manual until the evidence-link traversal is mechanically checked.

claims.statement: Evidence that predates the current spec revision is distinguishable from current evidence.
claims.rationale: Requires a seeded stale evidence state; default live reconciliation cannot make stale captures reachable yet.

claims.statement: The no-captures state explains that BAS skips are not failures and how to produce a capture.
claims.rationale: v1 BAS reconciliation captures only the default state; this empty-state promise needs multi-state capture before it can be machine tier.

claims.statement: On desktop, screenshot and accessibility tree are jointly visible without tab switching.
claims.rationale: Layout-level intent; candidate for the P2 perception tier or a viewport-scoped structural check.
